cards.title: 2.1.1 Motion, Frame of Reference and Coordinate System
body: Birds fly, fish swim, blood flows through veins and arteries and cars move.
Atoms, molecules, planets, and stars are all in motion.
Buses transport people from one place to another.
Aeoroplanes fly from one place to another.

cards.title: 2.1.2 Distance and Displacement
body: A learner said to his friend that he walks about 2 km from his home to school.
In everyday language, the terms distance and displacement are used in the same sense.
Definitely he is 200 m – 60 m = 140 m east of his initial position.
The change in position during a given time interval is called displacement.

cards.title: 2.1.3 Speed and Velocity
body: In everyday language, people use the terms speed and velocity interchangeably just as they use the words distance and displacement.
In physics speed and velocity have different meanings.
Speed is defined as the distance travelled per unit time.
The SI unit for speed is the metres per second (m/s or m.s-1).

cards.title: 2.1.4 Acceleration
body: For example, a car may start from rest, speed up to 60 km/h, remain at that velocity for some time, then slow down and finally stop.
A body moving with changing velocity is said to have acceleration.
Motion in which the velocity changes is known as non-uniform or accelerated motion.
Acceleration is the rate-of-change of velocity.

cards.title: 2.1.5 Uniformly Accelerated Motion
body: Sometimes an accelerating object will change its velocity by the same amount each second.
An object with a constant acceleration should not be confused with an object with a constant velocity.
If an object is changing its velocity – whether by a constant amount or a varying amount it is said to be accelerating.
An object with a constant velocity is not accelerating.

cards.title: 2.1.6 Equations of Uniformly Accelerated Motion
body: For motions with constant acceleration the average acceleration is equal to the constant acceleration.
Replacing aav by the constant acceleration a in Eq.
The average velocity can be calculated as: (6 m/s + 8 m/s + 10 m/s + 12 m/s + 14 m/s)/5 10 m/s, or in a simple way as (6.0 m/s + 14 m/s )/2 = 10 m/s.
Solution: The velocity of the car, found from Eq.

cards.title: 2.1.7 Freely Falling Objects
body: An object thrown upwards falls back down because there are forces of gravity and air resistance acting on it.
In air, heavy objects fall faster than very light objects: in a vacuum, they fall at the same rate.
The difference is due to the effect of air resistance being greater on light bodies than on heavy ones.
A standard demonstration to show the rate of fall is that of a coin and paper demonstration.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: A person walks $$200\text{ m}$$ to the East, then turns around and walks $$60\text{ m}$$ to the West. What is the magnitude of the person's displacement?

steps.text: **Given:** Initial displacement $$x_1 = +200\text{ m}$$ (taking East as positive), subsequent displacement $$x_2 = -60\text{ m}$$ (West).
**Formula:** $$\Delta x = x_1 + x_2$$
**Substitution:** $$\Delta x = 200\text{ m} + (-60\text{ m}) = 140\text{ m}$$.
**Final Result:** The magnitude of the displacement is **$$140\text{ m}$$**.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: Zahra travels by car a total distance of $$640\text{ km}$$ in $$8\text{ h}$$. What was her average speed?

steps.text: **Given:** Total distance $$s = 640\text{ km}$$, total time taken $$t = 8\text{ h}$$.
**Formula:** $$v_{av} = \frac{s}{t}$$
**Substitution:** $$v_{av} = \frac{640\text{ km}}{8\text{ h}} = 80\text{ km/h}$$.
**Final Result:** The average speed is **$$80\text{ km/h}$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The speedometer of a car gives a reading of the car's:
cards.why:
**Given:** Speedometer reading of a moving car.

**Formula:** The speedometer shows the rate of travel at one specific moment in time without indicating direction.

**Substitution:** Speed at a specific instant is called instantaneous speed. Velocity requires direction, and average values require an interval, which a speedometer does not calculate directly.

**Final Result:** The correct option is **C. Instantaneous speed**.

cards.title: 2.2.1 Distance-time Graph for Motion with Uniform Velocity
body: A body travelling with uniform velocity covers equal distances, in a specified direction, in equal times.
For example, a motor cycle moving at a uniform velocity of 5m/s travels a distance of 5 m in 1 s, 10 m in 2 s, 15 m in 3 s and so on.
In time ‘t’ seconds it would cover a distance of ‘5t’ m.
When the distance travelled by a body is plotted against time the graph obtained is a distance-time graph.

cards.title: 2.2.2 Velocity-time Graph for Motion with Uniform Velocity
body: The velocity-time graph for motion with uniform velocity is a horizontal line, that is, a line parallel to the time axis.
The slope in a velocity-time graph represents acceleration.

body: As time passes the distance increases faster and faster.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: An object moving under the influence of gravity alone is said to be in:
cards.why:
**Given:** Object moving solely under gravitational force.

**Formula:** By definition, an object moving under gravity without air resistance or other forces is experiencing free fall.

**Substitution:** Since the only force is gravity, the object accelerates downward at $$g$$. This motion is defined as free fall.

**Final Result:** The correct option is **B. Free fall**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The velocity-time graph of an object moving with a uniform constant velocity is a:

options.C: C. Horizontal straight line parallel to the time axis
options.D: D. Sloping straight line passing through the origin

cards.why:
**Given:** Uniform constant velocity motion.

**Formula:** On a $$v-t$$ graph, the y-axis represents velocity. If velocity is constant, its value does not change over time.

**Substitution:** A constant y-value results in a flat horizontal line with a slope of zero, parallel to the horizontal time axis.

**Final Result:** The correct option is **C. Horizontal straight line parallel to the time axis**.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The velocity-time graph of an object moving with a uniform constant velocity is a:

steps.text: **Given:** Uniform constant velocity motion.
**Formula:** On a $$v-t$$ graph, the y-axis represents velocity. If velocity is constant, its value does not change over time.
**Substitution:** A constant y-value results in a flat horizontal line with a slope of zero, parallel to the horizontal time axis.
**Final Result:** The correct option is **C. Horizontal straight line parallel to the time axis**.

cards.answer: C. Horizontal straight line parallel to the time axis

glossary.meaning: Kinematics is the description of how objects move and dynamics deals with why objects move as they do.
Motion is a continuous change of position (or location) with time.
Displacement is the final (new) position minus the initial (old) position.
Speed is defined as the distance travelled per unit time.
Acceleration is the rate-of-change of velocity.
Distance is the total length of the path followed.

tips.text: Every body in the universe is in motion.
Motion is a continuous change of position (or location) with time.
The position of an object is its location relative to a reference point.
As an object moves it covers a certain distance.
Distance is the total length of the path followed.
A vector quantity related to distance is the displacement of a body in motion.
Displacement is the straight line distance in a specific direction.
Speed is the distance travelled per unit time whereas velocity is the displacement per unit time.
Speed is a scalar quantity whereas velocity is a vector quantity.

When the velocity of a body remains constant, then the motion is known as uniform motion. However, when the velocity changes in magnitude or direction, the motion is said to be accelerated motion and the object possesses accelerations.
Motion in one dimension: v=u+at s=ut+½at² v²=u²+2as s = displacement. Free fall: a=±g. v–t slope = a; area under v–t = displacement.

similar.q: Two baseballs are thrown from the roof of a house with the same initial speed; one is thrown up and the other is thrown down. Compare the speeds of the baseballs just before they hit the ground.  A) The one thrown up has higher speed because the initial velocity is up.  B) The one thrown down has higher speed because the initial velocity is down.  C) They both have the same speed.  D) The one thrown up has higher speed because it has greater acceleration.  E) The one thrown down has higher speed because it has greater acceleration.
similar.a: C. They both have the same speed. — Energy view: same initial KE and same loss of PE → same final KE. The ball thrown up returns to the roof with its initial speed, now downward, and then repeats the other ball's motion. Answer: C.
